signals.fact: Some new insurance products and customer experience features have had mixed reception.
signals.challenge: Fit and trust may be the problem, not delivery speed.
signals.response: Analyse by customer moment, product, market and service outcome.
signals.proof: Comprehension, qualified starts, bind, service contacts and complaints.

signals.fact: Some Albanian customers still expect a physical vehicle and paperwork, despite an in-app journey.
signals.challenge: Digital completion does not prove that customers trust the cover.
signals.response: Give customers verifiable status, printable proof and human help.
signals.proof: Proof retrieval, print requests, verification and ‘am I covered?’ contacts.

signals.fact: 6M 2026 insurance revenue grew 59.6%. Standalone motor and health were targeted for later in 2026.
signals.challenge: Standalone products add discovery, renewal, service and claims work.
signals.response: Use one journey: discover, understand, activate, prove, use and renew.
signals.proof: Incremental adoption and renewal, with complaint, exception and economic guardrails.

stages.label: Why now
stages.customerOutcome: I understand why this offer is relevant. I can dismiss it.
stages.decision: Explain the trigger before asking for attention.
stages.evidence: Qualified detail views; dismissals; downstream bind by entry context.
stages.control: Use only approved or customer-declared context. Never imply certainty.
stages.challenge: A product shelf creates visibility, not relevance.

stages.label: Build cover
stages.customerOutcome: I can see what changes between options in situations I recognise.
stages.decision: Compare outcomes first; price and policy language second.
stages.evidence: Option changes; comparison opens; quote-to-review progression.
stages.control: Carrier-approved wording, eligibility and price remain deterministic.
stages.challenge: Insurance labels are easy to scan and hard to understand.

stages.label: Know the cover
stages.customerOutcome: I know what is covered, what is not and where limits apply.
stages.decision: Use three concrete scenarios and preserve full policy access.
stages.evidence: Scenario expands; exclusions opens; correction and abandonment points.
stages.control: No generated policy wording. Version every disclosure accepted.
stages.challenge: Fast checkout can leave the customer unsure what is covered.

stages.label: Issue safely
stages.customerOutcome: I know my money is safe, my cover is not active and what happens next.
stages.decision: Separate payment success from policy activation. Suppress repeat payment.
stages.evidence: Exception age; duplicate attempts; support contact; time to resolution.
stages.control: One transaction ID, reconciliation owner, SLA timer and escalation path.
stages.challenge: Payment can succeed while carrier issuance fails or times out.

stages.label: Prove cover
stages.customerOutcome: I can verify, download or print proof. I know who carries the risk.
stages.decision: Make active status and evidence more prominent than product promotion.
stages.evidence: Wallet opens; verification; downloads; print requests; service contacts.
stages.control: Status comes from policy records, not front-end assumption.
stages.challenge: Trust is tested after purchase, often outside the original channel.

stages.label: Get help
stages.customerOutcome: I can report the incident once and see who owns the next step.
stages.decision: Ask only for evidence needed now; expose hand-offs and status.
stages.evidence: Completion; evidence rework; status checks; time to first response.
stages.control: A person handles vulnerable, disputed or unclear cases.
stages.challenge: Partner hand-offs can make the customer repeat the story.

loop.title: Observe
loop.question: Where does the customer stop or ask for help?
loop.input: Journey events, exception queues, service reasons, complaints and claim cases.
loop.action: Cut by market, product, entry context, carrier and journey version.
loop.exit: A bounded problem with an affected cohort and baseline.

loop.title: Diagnose
loop.question: Is it relevance, comprehension, trust or operations?
loop.input: Behavioural funnel plus customer and frontline evidence.
loop.action: Trace the failure across customer, Iute and carrier. Do not stop at the screen.
loop.exit: A causal hypothesis and the evidence that could disprove it.

loop.title: Decide
loop.question: What is the smallest valuable intervention?
loop.input: Expected customer value, economics, operational load and risk.
loop.action: Write the decision, owner, guardrail and rollback condition.

loop.title: Instrument
loop.question: What must be knowable on day one?
loop.input: Primary outcome, guardrails and failure states.
loop.action: Define event, state, version and reconciliation evidence before build.
loop.exit: A testable release with no critical blind spot.

loop.title: Release
loop.question: Can this fail safely?
loop.input: Launch gates, monitoring, support readiness and carrier SLA.
loop.action: Stage exposure; rehearse exceptions; keep a kill switch and accountable owner.

loop.title: Learn
loop.question: Did behaviour, trust and economics move together?
loop.input: Experiment result, cohort quality, operations and customer evidence.
loop.action: Scale, revise or stop. Record the reason and the result.
loop.exit: A proven shared component or a documented local exception.
